remediation.suggestion: Include the helper script or document the required trusted tool and expected path clearly.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work can produce fragile formulas, inconsistent formats, and hidden calculation errors. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safer Excel workbook creation.
actual_capabilities: Creates basic .xlsx workbooks with openpyxl examples.
Shows how to preserve formulas when reading Excel files.
Applies financial model color coding and number formats.
Edits existing workbooks by changing cells, rows, columns, and sheets.
Explains formula recalculation and common Excel error checks.
Provides library guidance for pandas and openpyxl workflows.
limitations: It does not include a complete recalculation script in the scanned files.
It cannot calculate Excel formulas directly through openpyxl.
It assumes users already have trusted spreadsheet files and Python libraries.
It gives examples, not a full application for spreadsheet uploads or storage.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create an Excel workbook with formula-driven metrics, color-coded inputs, and clear number formats.

use_cases.title: Clean Workbook Inputs
use_cases.description: Read sheets with pandas or openpyxl, map columns, and prepare workbook data for analysis.

use_cases.title: Validate Spreadsheet Outputs
use_cases.description: Check formulas, cross-sheet references, and common Excel error types before sharing a workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook with columns for metric, year, value, and notes. Use formulas where totals are needed, not hardcoded sums.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Financial Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook with standard financial model colors, currency formats, percentage formats, and wider columns for readable labels.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the existing workbook, add an Analysis sheet, link it to the Data sheet, and preserve formulas when saving the edited file.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Formula Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the workbook for #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, and #NAME? errors. Explain the likely cause of each issue and recommend fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a revenue model with revenue, growth, and projected next year revenue.
output_examples.output: A workbook is created with labeled rows, blue input cells, black formula cells, currency formatting, and formulas for growth-based projections.

output_examples.input: Check why my workbook has formula errors after deleting columns.
output_examples.output: The review identifies likely broken references, explains where #REF! errors usually appear, and recommends updating formulas before sharing the file.

output_examples.input: Read all worksheets and summarize which library to use.
output_examples.output: The guidance recommends pandas for analysis, openpyxl for formula preservation, and read-only mode for large workbook inspection.

best_practices: Use Excel formulas for calculated values so workbooks remain auditable.
Apply consistent colors for inputs, formulas, links, and external references.
Verify formulas and common error types after editing workbook structure.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode calculated totals when an Excel formula should remain visible.
Do not save a data-only workbook when formulas must be preserved.
Do not ignore cross-sheet references after inserting or deleting rows and columns.

faq.question: What files does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on .xlsx Excel workbooks and Python workflows using openpyxl and pandas.

faq.question: Can it calculate Excel formulas by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains that openpyxl writes formulas but does not calculate their values.

faq.question: Does it help with financial model formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes color standards for inputs, formulas, worksheet links, and external file links.

faq.question: Can it edit existing spreadsheets?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to load a workbook, modify cells, add sheets, and save a new file.

faq.question: Does it include validation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists checks for formula references, division by zero, value errors, and unknown functions.

faq.question: Is it only for finance teams?
faq.answer: No. Finance examples are central, but the same patterns help analysts and operations teams manage Excel files.
